css:
/* NO @font-face HERE — ON PURPOSE.

   THE CONTRACT
   For server-generated bERP PDFs using the supported wkhtmltopdf rendering
   stack, Lao typography MUST NOT depend on CSS @font-face. The required Lao
   static font faces MUST be installed in the server font environment and
   resolvable through fontconfig. Print CSS MAY specify the corresponding
   font-family, but MUST NOT embed or override those Lao faces with @font-face.

   WHY
   Measured on wkhtmltopdf 0.12.6, same HTML, only the @font-face block
   differing, fonts installed on the machine in both runs:

       with @font-face        embedded: DejaVuSans          text: "—"
       without, font present  embedded: Phetsarath-Regular  text: ໜຶ່ງລ້ານສອງແສນກີບຖ້ວນ

   This is a statement about this rendering stack, not about every wkhtmltopdf
   build. @font-face is reported to work for some fonts and fail for others
   across versions, file formats and platforms; that inconsistency is itself the
   reason not to make it part of the production contract.

   SEVERITY
   Not a typography defect. DejaVu covers the Lao block, so a missing font does
   not produce boxes — it produces Lao that is visually plausible with the
   combining marks in the wrong order (ໜຶງ່ for ໜຶ່ງ). The document still looks
   valid. Treat this as document integrity / regulatory presentation risk, and
   note that "characters rendered" is therefore not a success criterion.

   OPERATING IT
   Run scripts/install-lao-fonts.sh on every machine that renders PDFs.
   berp_lao.lao_regional.fonts.font_status() reports READY / MISSING / UNKNOWN. */

.print-format,
.print-format * {
	font-family: "Phetsarath", "Noto Sans Lao", "Saysettha OT", serif;
}
